page: Microsoft Azure FX32-16mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-intensive virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, providing 8 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs. The hardware configuration features an exceptionally high memory allocation of 672.0 GB RAM (42.0 GB per vCPU), supported by a substantial 260 MB L3 cache. In addition to high compute and memory capacity, the instance includes 1888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and lacks discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compute and text-handling capabilities. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2315.0 and a text processing score of 2959.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded data handling is reinforced by strong throughput in gzip compression (34.78 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.22 GB/sec). Memory subsystems show strong large-block uncached write bandwidth at 91.91 GB/sec, while cached read speeds reach 1392.74 GB/sec. Across multi-core benchmarks, the instance yields mid-tier results, reflecting its 16-vCPU footprint against larger-scale multi-socket profiles.

The combination of a high clock speed, an exceptionally dense memory footprint, and local NVMe storage targets workloads constrained by single-thread frequency and RAM capacity rather than raw core scaling. Best-fit use cases include electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory databases, large-scale financial modeling, compilation tasks, and data engineering pipelines requiring expansive local scratch space.
